bestPractices.title: BMP Compression Best Practices
bestPractices.description: Follow these expert tips to get the best results when working with BMP files.

tips.title: Understand BMP's Legacy Role
tips.content: BMP is an uncompressed or minimally compressed (RLE) format from the Windows era. It produces large files (2-10x larger than PNG, 5-20x larger than JPEG) but offers universal compatibility with legacy systems. Use BMP only when specifically required by older software, hardware, or system requirements.

tips.title: Convert to Modern Formats
tips.content: For 99% of use cases, convert BMP to modern formats: PNG for lossless compression (50-70% smaller, perfect for screenshots and graphics), JPEG for photos (80-95% smaller), or WebP for best overall compression (70-90% smaller). This dramatically reduces storage and bandwidth requirements while maintaining or improving quality.

tips.title: Optimize Color Depth If Staying BMP
tips.content: If BMP format is mandatory, reduce color depth based on content: use 8-bit (256 colors) for simple graphics, 4-bit (16 colors) for very simple images, or 1-bit for black and white. Enable RLE compression for 4-bit and 8-bit images with large solid-color areas—can achieve 30-60% size reduction for suitable images.

tips.title: Strategic Batch Conversion
tips.content: When migrating from legacy BMP-based systems, batch convert to appropriate formats: PNG for UI graphics and screenshots, JPEG quality 85-90 for photos, WebP for modern web applications. Test converted files thoroughly with target applications before replacing originals. Maintain BMP backups only if absolutely necessary for legacy compatibility.

items.question: What is BMP format used for?
items.answer: BMP (Bitmap) is primarily used for legacy system compatibility, simple graphics storage, and applications requiring uncompressed bitmap data. It's widely supported across all Windows applications but produces large file sizes compared to modern formats.

items.question: How much can BMP files be compressed?
items.answer: Native BMP compression (RLE) typically achieves 20-50% size reduction for simple graphics. However, converting BMP to modern formats like PNG can achieve 50-70% reduction, while conversion to WebP can achieve 70-90% reduction.

items.question: Should I use BMP for photos or web images?
items.answer: No. BMP produces very large file sizes and is unsuitable for web use or photo storage. Use JPEG for photos, PNG for graphics with transparency, or WebP for the best compression with excellent quality.

items.question: What's the difference between BMP and PNG?
items.answer: PNG offers far superior compression (typically 50-70% smaller) while being completely lossless like BMP. PNG also supports transparency, has better color management, and is optimized for web use. BMP's main advantage is universal legacy compatibility.
